newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad president falls short of parliament majority.
newsitem.headline: Chad president falls short of parliament majority.

text.p: President Idriss Deby fell short of an outright majority in Chad's parliamentary election, with the Moslem north and Christian south voting along regional lines, provisional results show.

Results of February run-offs, issued by the Independent National Electoral Commission late on Monday, must be confirmed by the appeal court but already there is talk of a coalition between supporters of Deby and Foreign Minister Saleh Kebzabo.

Deby, a former guerrilla leader from the Moslem north, and his ruling Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS) ended up with 55 of the 125 seats in the new national assembly after two rounds of voting on January 5 and on February 23.
His southern presidential rival, fellow general Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue, and his Union for Renewal and Democracy (URD) won 31 seats.
Kebzabo, a former journalist, and his National Union for Development and Renewal (UNDR) in the south west, won 15.

UNDR sources close say they signed an accord with Deby's party between the two rounds of voting on forming a majority. "If the agreement is respected then the two parties will have a majority of 70 seats in the national assembly," one said.

Deby seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup after decades of civil war or conflict with Libya. After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential election in July in a run-off against Kamougue.
Chad, a sprawling former French colony on the fringes of the Sahara desert, previously had a 57-member interim assembly under a 1993 transitional charter.
